title: Insteon command set
description: The settings and messages a family of Insteon products shares, in the Insteon protocol's own terms: operating flags read with Get Operating Flags (cmd1 0x1F) and set with Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20), values read and written with extended Get and Set (cmd1 0x2E), other standard and extended direct commands, and the direct messages the products send on their own. Profiles name the command sets their identities and firmware versions use.

id.description: The command set's identifier, which profiles name and the file is named for.

name.description: What people call the command set, such as the product family it comes from.

description.description: Which products use the command set, and what sets it apart.

displayScale.description: How to tell whether the device displays Celsius, for values in displayDegrees. Without it, or before it's been read, they're Fahrenheit.

celsiusWhen.description: An operating flag, value or named bit that is true when the device displays Celsius.

enumerations.description: Names for the values of a byte.

valueTables.description: Names for the values of settings, which values name with table.

operatingFlags.description: Bits of a Get Operating Flags reply, and the Set Operating Flags commands that change them.

readings.description: Get Operating Flags queries whose whole reply is a value rather than bits.

flagCommands.description: Set Operating Flags commands whose effect no Get Operating Flags bit is documented to show.

standardCommands.description: Standard direct commands beyond the operating flags.

extendedCommands.description: Extended direct commands beyond extended Get and Set with cmd2 0x00, such as a Get with another cmd2 and its reply.

directMessages.description: Standard direct messages the device sends on its own, such as a thermostat's reports.

groupTypes.description: What the device's groups are, which profiles name in their groups' type.

linkingChanges.description: The operating flags linking can change on its own, which a linking flow may read before it links and set back afterward: an allowlist. A linking flow changes and restores no other flag, and never one with a guard.

flag.description: The operating flag linking can change. It has both on and off, so a flow can set it back.

sources.description: The documents the values come from.

byte.description: A byte, written as 0x followed by two uppercase hexadecimal digits.

name.description: A name for code to refer to, in lower camel case.

description.description: What the flag means when its bit is 1.

query.description: The Get Operating Flags cmd2 whose reply holds the bit.

bit.description: The bit's mask in the reply's cmd2.

on.description: The Set Operating Flags cmd2 that sets the bit to 1.

off.description: The Set Operating Flags cmd2 that sets the bit to 0.

extendedWhen.description: An operating flag that, while set, has its Set Operating Flags commands sent as an extended message instead, with cmd1 and cmd2 again in D1 and D2 and the other user data bytes 0x00.

default.description: The bit's value as the device leaves the factory.

onCommand.description: A standard command that sets the bit, for a flag Set Operating Flags doesn't set.

offCommand.description: A standard command that clears the bit.

guard.description: How an app writing operating flags treats the bit, so it never cuts the device off, locks it or changes the message form it accepts: keep, a write leaves the bit as it was read, as for radio off, powerline off, checksum required and the thermostat adapter's extended commands only; neverSet, a write may clear the bit but never sets it, as for the programming lock. It holds for Set Operating Flags, for a write to a value whose flagsQuery names this flag's query, and for an extended command's flags parameter that holds the bit.

extendedWhen.description: An operating flag that, while set, has the command sent as an extended message instead, with cmd1 and cmd2 again in D1 and D2 and the other user data bytes 0x00.

guard.description: never: an app never sends the command, because it's a Set Operating Flags command (cmd1 0x20) that turns radio off, powerline off, checksum required or the programming lock on.

extendedSettings.description: Values read with an extended Get (cmd1 0x2E, D2 0x00) and written with an extended Set (D2 a selector). D1 is the button or group, or 0x01 for the whole device.

perButton.description: Whether D1 of a Get chooses a button or group whose values the reply holds.

values.description: The values in a Get reply, which has 0x01 in D2.

position.description: A user data byte, from D3 through D14.

flagsQuery.description: Marks the value as an operating flags byte: the byte Get Operating Flags returns for this query (cmd2), such as 0x00. Its bits are the command set's operatingFlags with that query, which name them and say which a write must guard.

kind.description: How to read the value: a number, or a mask with one bit per button, button 1 in bit 0.

default.description: The value as the device leaves the factory.

table.description: The value table that names each value, such as the ramp rate's durations.

unit.description: The value's unit once scaled, for a value shown as a number.

scale.description: What one count is worth in the value's unit, such as 100/255 for a level shown as a percentage.

write.description: The extended command that sets the value, for a value no extended Set write sets.

perButton.description: Whether D1 chooses the button or group the value is for. Otherwise D1 is ignored, and 0x01 is sent.

bytes.description: Which value goes in each byte from D3.

value.description: The name of a value, or of a value the Set alone writes.

dataByte.description: A user data byte, from D1 through D14.

field.description: A value in a message: in cmd2 of a standard message, or in user data bytes of an extended one, and how to read it.

byte.description: The user data byte that holds the value, in an extended message.

bytes.description: The user data bytes that hold the value, most significant first, in an extended message. They needn't be next to each other.

kind.description: How to read the value: a number, a mask with one bit per button (button 1 in bit 0), a name from an enumeration, named bits, or a boolean that is true when nonzero.

range.description: The values it can take, in its unit.

mask.description: The bits of the byte that hold the value. The value is shifted down past the mask's low zero bits.

signed.description: Whether the value is a two's complement number.

scale.description: What one count is worth in the value's unit, such as 0.5 for half degrees.

unit.description: The value's unit once scaled. displayDegrees are degrees in the scale the device displays, which the command set's displayScale says how to find.

enumeration.description: With kind enumeration, the enumeration that names each value.

bits.description: With kind flags, the named bits.

guard.description: For a flags parameter an app writes, how the write treats the bit: keep, it leaves the bit as the device last reported it; neverSet, it may clear the bit but never sets it. The same as the guard of the operating flag the bit mirrors.

integrity.description: How an extended message's user data is protected: none; a checksum in D14, the two's complement of the sum of cmd1, cmd2 and D1 through D13; or a CRC over cmd1, cmd2 and D1 through D12, with its high byte in D13 and its low byte in D14.

standardCommand.description: A standard direct command: cmd1, and a fixed cmd2 or one the caller gives. With neither, cmd2 is 0x00.

parameter.description: The value the caller gives in cmd2, instead of a fixed one.

reply.description: The value the acknowledgment carries in cmd2.

extendedWhen.description: An operating flag that, while set, has the command sent as an extended message instead, with cmd1 and cmd2 again in D1 and D2 and the other user data bytes 0x00.

followUp.description: A value that one more standard direct message with the same cmd1 may carry after the acknowledgment, such as a second setpoint. The device sends it only when it has that value.

guard.description: never: an app never sends the command, because it's a Set Operating Flags command (cmd1 0x20) that turns radio off, powerline off, checksum required or the programming lock on.

extendedCommand.description: An extended direct command: cmd1, cmd2 and user data the caller fills in, and the extended reply that carries values back, if any.

perButton.description: Whether D1 chooses a button or group.

fixed.description: The command's fixed user data bytes. The rest are 0x00, apart from parameters and integrity.

parameters.description: The values the caller gives, and the bytes each goes in.

reply.description: The extended direct message that answers the command, after its acknowledgment.

command1.description: The reply's cmd1. Defaults to the command's.

match.description: Bytes that tell this reply apart from others with the same command.

guard.description: never: an app never sends the command, because it's a Set Operating Flags command (cmd1 0x20) that turns radio off, powerline off, checksum required or the programming lock on.

directMessage.description: A standard direct message the device sends on its own, with a value in cmd2.

verification.description: How the catalog knows the value. Omitted means documented: an Insteon document gives it and none of the catalog's sources disagree.

status.description: documented: an Insteon document gives the value, as when the field is omitted, and the note says more. inferred: no document states it; it's read from an example, a similar product or the product's behavior, as the note explains. conflicting: Insteon's documents disagree; the note says what each gives, and the value is the one the catalog uses. observed: the value has been seen on a device, running the firmware versions listed; the note says what was seen.

note.description: What the status rests on: the documents and what each says, or what was observed.

firmware.description: For observed values, the firmware versions the devices it was seen on were running.

label.description: What a settings page calls the item, in sentence case, such as Key beep.

section.description: The heading a settings page shows the item under. Apps show the sections in this order.

advanced.description: Whether a settings page should keep the item out of sight unless asked, such as a setting for testing or for the powerline's timing.

valueTable.description: Names for the values of a setting whose raw values mean something else, such as ramp rates and the durations they stand for.

seconds.description: The duration the value stands for, in seconds.

groupType.description: What a group of the device is, how to read its state and what it can be told to do.

kind.description: What it is: a dimmer, a relay or outlet switched on and off, a fan with speeds, a sensor or input that only reports, a button that controls other devices, a window covering or other motorized cover that opens and closes, an alarm that sounds when the device is armed in one of its armModes and a linked device triggers it, or an arming group that arms the device in its armModes.

command.description: The standard command whose acknowledgment carries the state.

bitPerGroup.description: Whether the reply holds one bit per group, group 1 in bit 0, rather than the state itself.

ranges.description: Names for ranges of the reply's value, such as a fan's speeds.

onWhen.description: For a group whose state is a pattern of bits in a status byte the device's groups share, such as an EZFlora zone: the group is on when the reply's cmd2 ANDed with mask equals value, and off otherwise.

actions.description: What an app can tell the group to do, for controls, scenes and schedules. A group whose type has actions must be a responder.

command.description: The standard or extended command to send.

value.description: The value to give the command's parameter. Without it, the caller gives it, such as a dimmer's level.

schedulable.description: Whether the action makes sense in a schedule.

outputs.description: Outputs the group's load is made of, which one command can switch together: each action whose command takes a parameter, and gives no fixed value, selects outputs by their bits in it, so the bits of several outputs ORed together switch them all at once.

activeWhen.description: The operating flag state under which the load is these outputs, such as relay mode. Omitted, it always is.

armModes.description: For an alarm group, the armed modes in any of which a trigger from a linked device sounds it; for an arming group, the modes a group On from its controller arms the device in, all together.

linkData.description: What Data 1 to 3 of an ALL-Link database record hold for the group: in a responder's record, the state the group goes to when its controller's group command arrives; in a controller's record, what it keeps about the responder.

linkDataByte.description: What one data byte of an ALL-Link database record holds.

value.description: The value to write, when it's fixed, such as the FanLinc fan's button number.

table.description: The value table that names each value, such as the ramp rate's or on and off.

perGroup.description: Whether the byte is the responder's own group: the button or part of the device the record is for, as the profile group with this type numbers it. It isn't the record's Group field, which holds the controller's group.
